newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Sterling slips in Europe after soft UK data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sterling slips in Europe after soft UK data.

text.p: Sterling was down over two pfennigs against the mark from late Thursday levels by European midsession trade on Friday, driven lower by profit-taking following soft British manufacturing and industrial data.
"The weak data, particularly manufacturing, took the market by surprise," said a UK bank dealer. "The market is taking stock of how much a strong pound will affect the economy."

The Confederation of British Industry distributive trades survey for December released early Friday also put some pressure on the pound, showing retail sales volumes for last month were less than expected.

This latest CBI survey and other UK data has cooled some of the recent speculation of a near-term British interest rate rise, which some were expecting as soon as next week's monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
"There still is a risk of a rate rise, but it's a reduced risk from a week ago," said Tim Fox, economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
He sees a small near-term rate hike as sending the right signal to the marketplace but without disturbing the momentum of the economy.
The CBI survey showed a 33 percent positive balance of higher sales among firms surveyed, well below November's 48 percent.
UK manufacturing output, meantime, dipped 0.5 percent in November against a median forecast of a 0.3 percent rise while industrial production posted a 0.4 percent gain versus 0.5 percent forecast.
By 1200 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.6545 marks, well below Thursday's 52-month high of 2.6767 marks. It stood at $1.6828 compared with $1.6963 late Thursday in Europe.
Dealers said an article in the Times newspaper also put some early pressure on the pound.
The article was fairly bullish on British growth prospects but cautioned against the pound's ability to clear the $1.70 level against the backdrop of a strengthening dollar/mark.
Sterling/mark's uptrend, by contrast, was expected to continue, according to the article.
The Times article provided some early influence, said dealers. "But it comes at a convenient time for people to start booking profits, and that's exactly what we've seen," said the UK bank dealer.
